jobs.title: Solutions Engineer
jobs.description:
About Code Metal

Code Metal is the leader in automated software engineering you can trust. As AI writes more of the world's code, the bottleneck in software has shifted from writing code to verifying it works, and AI cannot verify its own work with certainty. Code Metal takes a fundamentally different approach: constrain AI to what it does reliably, verify every step independently of the model using formal methods, and keep engineers in the loop on the decisions that matter. The result isn't code that probably works — it's code that is provably correct, with auditable proof. Customers including the U.S. Air Force, L3Harris, RTX, and Toshiba use Code Metal to modernize legacy code, optimize performance on real hardware, and move prototypes to production, fast. Founded in 2023 with offices in Boston and San Francisco, Code Metal is funded by Accel, Salesforce Ventures, B Capital, Smith Point Capital, J2 Ventures, Shield Capital, Overmatch, RTX, and others.

Learn more at codemetal.ai.

Solutions Engineer

Code Metal is looking for a Solutions Engineer to sit at the intersection of engineering, prototyping, and customer growth - turning promising opportunities into working technical systems. You'll be a hands-on bridge between our platform and real-world use, building and validating customer solutions through proofs of concept and early development, then helping transition successful work toward repeatable production use.

Who thrives in this role:

Engineers who enjoy turning loosely defined customer problems into working systems.
Technically curious people who can quickly explore unfamiliar domains, prototype approaches, and turn what they learn into working solutions.
Hands-on builders who combine strong technical judgment with rapid execution and follow-through.
Comfortable owning the technical execution of a customer problem - from a scoped opportunity through a validated proof of concept and early deployment.
Thrive in open-ended environments and can context-switch quickly across technical domains.
Willing to learn quickly and go deep when a customer problem demands it.
A strong technical background is required, whether your experience comes from engineering, research, or other technical roles. You'll often be among the first engineers to prove how Code Metal's technology can solve a new customer problem in practice.

Responsibilities:

Turn scoped customer opportunities into working technical solutions that demonstrate how Code Metal's technology can be applied in real-world systems.
Work with customer engineers and stakeholders to understand development needs, system constraints, and success criteria, then translate them into executable implementation plans.
Rapidly investigate unfamiliar technical domains and de-risk solution paths through hands-on prototyping, integration, and feasibility testing.
Build and lead proofs of concept (PoCs), working with Solutions Architects, product, engineering, and customer teams to turn an agreed approach into a validated system.
Implement complex algorithms and compute-heavy pipelines (DSP, RF, communications, and similar workloads) on GPUs, FPGAs, and edge systems using Code Metal's platform.
Profile, debug, and tune PoCs and early deployments for latency, throughput, memory, and power across heterogeneous compute environments.
Debug across heterogeneous systems (CPU/GPU/FPGA), identifying and resolving issues spanning algorithms, software, hardware, and toolchains.
Use PoCs and technical demos to make Code Metal's product differentiators concrete and measurable for customers.
Capture reusable code, integration patterns, and playbooks from successful PoCs so future customer work can move faster.
Support early integration and validation as needed, partnering with Forward Deployed Engineers when work transitions into sustained deployment or production.
Work across Solutions Architecture, Forward Deployed Engineering, product, core engineering, research, and growth, feeding technical learnings back into the platform and customer strategy.

Requirements:

Strong background in computer science, systems engineering, electrical engineering, physics, or a related technical field.
Ability to quickly learn unfamiliar domains and turn new technical information into practical experiments and implementations.
Strong analytical thinking, problem decomposition, and hands-on prototyping skills.
Demonstrated ability to debug complex systems across software and hardware boundaries.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain implementation tradeoffs and technical results clearly to customers and internal teams.
Self-starter who can operate independently and effectively in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
Willingness to travel occasionally to customer sites as needed (est. 10%-20% travel)

Great to Have:

Experience designing or architecting complex technical systems.
Broad cross-domain software experience in one or more of: C/C++, Rust, Python, Verilog/VHDL, MATLAB, CUDA/OpenCL.
Hands-on experience with GPU programming, FPGA development, embedded or edge systems, especially where software, hardware, and physical systems intersect.
Experience with compute-intensive workloads such as DSP, RF, communications, or computer vision.
Experience working with U.S. Government programs or dual-use technologies.
Active U.S. security clearance (Secret or Top Secret), or eligibility to obtain one.

Level Expectations by Track

This role is open at Senior, Staff, or Principal level. The expectations below describe how scope, ownership, and technical leadership differ by level; candidates are evaluated against the level they are hired into.

Senior:

Years of Experience: 5+
Engineering Craft & Code Quality: Writes clean, idiomatic, well-tested code/output and follows best practices; drives debugging of the team's hardest issues; ensures AI-assisted work is correct, modular, and fully tested.
Architecture & Technical Knowledge: Designs and implements changes to single systems, collaborates on larger designs, and drives architecture reviews for multi-developer projects.
Delivery, Scoping & De-risking: Works with Product to scope and de-risk work; provides reliable estimates for medium-sized projects with clear risk communication.
Technical Leadership & Mentorship: A go-to technical reviewer for the team's codebase; mentors and onboards teammates; contributes to interviews and candidate experience.

Staff:

Years of Experience: 7+
Engineering Craft & Code Quality: Defines and enforces the team's testing strategy, standards, and quality bar; ensures AI-generated output is tightly integrated into existing paradigms and robustly tested.
Architecture & Technical Knowledge: Designs cross-cutting changes across the stack; provides architectural guidance across the team; owns design docs for major multi-service or multi-surface projects.
Delivery, Scoping & De-risking: Owns technical scoping and execution strategy for complex, multi-sprint initiatives; audits requirements for technical risk and hidden dependencies before development begins.
Technical Leadership & Mentorship: The primary technical gatekeeper for the team's codebase; reviews most high-impact work; leads technical grooming, design spikes, and RFCs; coordinates across pods when changes cross domain boundaries.

Principal:

Years of Experience: 10+
Engineering Craft & Code Quality: Sets the quality and correctness bar across the department; their work is the example others learn from; improves the automated systems and practices that ensure quality department-wide.
Architecture & Technical Knowledge: Provides architectural guidance across the department and invents paradigms that solve CodeMetal-specific domain problems (e.g., translation, optimization, deployment across target environments); a key resource on every major system.
Delivery, Scoping & De-risking: A consistent contributor to the company's technical roadmap; gives reliable estimates for large cross-team initiatives; ensures pragmatic scoping toward the most valuable outcomes.
Technical Leadership & Mentorship: An active driver of company-wide architectural reviews and proposals; mentors mid-level and senior staff at scale; influences others across departments toward the best technical outcome.

Benefits

Pay depends on experience, but we strive to be at the upper end of the salary range
Health care plan with 100% premium coverage, including medical, dental, and vision
401k with 5% matching
Paid Time Off (uncapped vacation, plus sick and public holidays)
Flexible hybrid or remote work arrangement
Relocation assistance for qualifying employees

Wage Transparency - The salary range for this role is not a guarantee of compensation or salary, as the final offer amount may vary based on factors including, but not limited to, individual proficiency, skills, experience, and location.

We are an equal opportunity employer. US Citizenship may be required for certain project assignments involving security clearance.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Description

Eastern Shawnee Companies, LLC (ESC), is a board-governed holding company that proudly represents a collection of tribally owned small businesses providing professional and construction services. As a wholly owned subsidiary of the Eastern Shawnee Tribe of Oklahoma (ESTO), ESC is deeply committed to enhancing and supporting tribal sovereignty while delivering sustainable solutions for our diverse range of tribal, federal, government, and private clients.

Our primary focus is empowering tribal communities and promoting economic growth through dedicated services. By leveraging our experience and deep understanding of the challenges faced by tribal entities, ESC aims to be a trusted partner for tribal, federal, municipal, and private clients alike. We are passionate about creating sustainable solutions that benefit our clients and contribute to preserving tribal heritage and the well-being of future generations.

We invite you to join us on this transformative journey as we build upon tradition, empower communities, and create a legacy that resonates for future generations.

We are seeking a Environmental Field Technician to support environmental field activities in Fairchild, WA. This role involves conducting fieldwork, including groundwater monitoring and sampling, data collection, preparing field instruments and reporting. This role is not a regular full-time position, and work is available based on project requirements.

Requirements

Responsibilities:

Assist with inventory, calibration, and QC documentation of field instruments (PID, dissolved oxygen meter, multi-parameter water quality sonde, interface probe) and sampling supplies
Assist with staging, loading, and organizing field equipment, PPE, and sample coolers
Locate and access monitoring wells using site maps and GPS; document well surface conditions and integrity
Measure depth to groundwater and total well depth using an electronic water level meter
Purge monitoring wells using low-flow or standard purge methods per project SOPs, tracking water quality stabilization parameters
Collect groundwater samples for laboratory analysis following low-flow protocols
Clean re-usable sampling equipment in accordance with project SOPs
Maintain sample integrity through proper handling, preservation, and temperature control

Qualifications

HAZWOPER 40-hour certification (per 29 CFR 1910.120)
Annual 8-hour HAZWOPER refresher (if applicable)
Current medical clearance
Valid driver’s license (for travel between wells/sites)
Ability to obtain federal installation access badges (DBIDS/EAL badges)
First Aid/CPR certification (preferred but not required)
0–2+ years environmental field experience
Experience with environmental sampling, laboratory coordination, or field equipment calibration (preferred but not required)
Prior experience conducting (preferred but not required):
Groundwater sampling
Well purging and stabilization
Environmental data documentation and QC

Ability to work outdoors in varying weather conditions
Physical ability to lift equipment, traverse uneven terrain, and work long field days

Compensation.
The hourly range for this position is between $25 to $28. The actual hourly rate offered depends on factors, including but not limited to, qualifications, years of relevant experience, skills, education, certifications, business need, and market demand. This is not a benefit eligible position.

Job Summary

Galapagos Federal Systems, LLC is seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Data Analyst to join our team at Patrick Space Force Base, Florida. This position offers an exciting opportunity to support the Space Training and Readiness Command (STARCOM) by providing data analysis, reporting, and visualizations to improve operational effectiveness, and support mission success.

The Data Analyst will collect, analyze, and interpret data from multiple enterprise systems to develop workforce analysis, and support enterprise decisions making. The successful candidate will develop reports, dashboards, and data visualizations that provide meaningful insights to government stakeholders. This role requires strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and the ability to communicate technical information effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Key Responsibilities

The Data Analyst will

Develop and continuously enhance STARCOM's workforce analytics capabilities, providing timely, accurate, and actionable insights to support strategic decision-making
Analyze workforce, operational, and organizational data to identify trends, measure performance, and support planning efforts
Develop, maintain, and enhance executive dashboards, reports, and data visualizations using data from multiple enterprise systems
Design and implement automated reporting solutions, databases, and analytics tools to improve efficiency and data accessibility
Identify workforce trends, hiring metrics, readiness indicators, and organizational performance measures to inform leadership decisions
Collaborate with government stakeholders to gather requirements and develop reporting and analytical solutions
Respond to leadership and stakeholder requests by preparing timely, accurate reports, dashboards, and analytical products
Validate, integrate, cleanse, and standardize data from multiple sources to ensure data quality and consistency
Identify opportunities to improve reporting processes and recommend enhancements that increase efficiency
Prepare reports, presentations, and data visualizations that communicate analytical findings to technical and non-technical audiences
Develop predictive models and trend analyses to support workforce planning, forecasting, and data-driven decision-making

Skills And Experience

The Data Analyst must have

Active Top Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) security clearance
5+ years of experience supporting Department of Defense (DoD) organizations in data analytics, business intelligence, workforce analytics, or a related field
Demonstrated experience collecting, integrating, cleansing, validating, and analyzing large datasets from multiple enterprise systems
Experience developing executive dashboards, reports, and data visualizations using Microsoft Power BI, Power Apps, Excel, or similar business intelligence tools
Experience analyzing business processes, workforce data, and operational metrics to deliver actionable insights and recommendations
Experience collaborating with stakeholders to gather business requirements and develop data-driven analytical solutions
Experience implementing predictive analytics, forecasting models, and trend analysis to support strategic planning and organizational decision-making
Strong understanding of data quality management, governance, and data validation best practices
Ability to work independently while managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced, mission-focused environment

Must be a U.S. Citizen. A high-level Department of Defense active security clearance is/may be required. Applicants selected will be subject to a security investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements for access to government information.

Physical Requirements

Work may involve sitting or standing for extended periods of time and typing and reading from a computer screen. The candidate must have enough mobility, including bending, reaching, and kneeling, to complete daily duties in a prompt and efficient manner, and that may include lifting up to thirty pounds, as necessary.

Position Details

General Statement

Health Professions Resource Center (HPRC) is a pre-professional advising office that supports MSU students and alumni of any college of degree program. The office provides critical professional support within the areas of exploration, preparation, and application to health and allied health programs. The HPRC office focuses on individualized support plans for each student that guide their academic and professional journey during and after their time at Montana State University.

HPRC is also home to the post-bacc pre-medical certificate program for students who are career changers and require a substantial amount of coursework to fulfill pre-requisites for their graduate school applications.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Student Success Coordinator is required to provide a high level of administrative support, customer service, and technical support to Health Professions Advising. The Student Success Coordinator will enhance the quality and effectiveness of undergraduate, post-bacc, and graduate student pre-professional support, services and experiences with high level advising and technical support to students, faculty, and staff. Responds and works with campus departments to resolve academic issues. Maintains student electronic files, keeping up-to-date with university procedures, interpreting university academic policy and providing academic advice to faculty and students. Other related office duties may be assigned.

The duties and responsibilities of the Academic Services Coordinator include the following:

Health Professions Program Coordinator

Serves as the primary point of contact with the MSU student service units including the Office of the Registrar, Office of Admissions, Student Employment Services, and Student Support Services.
Provide information and support to students considering a health profession as a future career.
Helps make students aware of campus-wide advising and other academic support services.
Helps students understand and follow academic policies, rules, and requirements.
Inform students of academic and student support services.
Process undergraduate student forms, including Add/Drop and Change of Curriculum.
Serve as office liaison with the HRPC team and Advising Commons.
Maintain office advising information and resources SharePoint.
Assist with office events, including Welcome Back Social, end of semester, and graduation events.
Assess coursework for incoming post-bacc students.
Conduct graduation audits, review graduation applications and certify students for graduation based on guidelines provided by the steering committee for post-bacc pre-med certification program.
Provide academic advising to post-bacc students (non-degree) and post-bacc pre-med certificate (degree) students.
Coordinate communication of information related to important dates, deadlines and procedures to advisees and staff within the academic unit(s) served.

Administration

Serves as front-line customer service; assists Director of HRPC, in day-to-day operations of the office.
Maintains schedules for conference rooms.
Researches and prepares data on academic issues such as course offerings, enrollment, and course loads to provide supporting documentation for critical pre-req courses for students.
Refer student issues or faculty questions to HRPC Director.
Manages FERPA form completion and letters of recommendation for students. Manages record of the file submission in Karatemail and updates internal databases.
Assist with the management of student data- entering students into banner for NAV and Degreeworks indicators, student meetings record, admissions data, etc.
Manages catalog revisions and course offerings in campus systems.

Communications/Events Coordinator

Creates departmental marketing and promotional materials in partnership with University Communications.
Manages and maintains web pages in accordance with university guidelines.
Assists with weekly newsletter to students, faculty, and MSU staff.

Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field with experience working with undergraduate college students in an academic or student support setting, or an equivalent combination of education and/or experience.
Experience working with academic curricula, degree requirements, policies and procedures in a higher education setting.
Progressively responsible experience providing customer service in an office environment or an equivalent combination of relevant education and/or experience.
Demonstrated excellent customer service and written and verbal communication skills to serve constituents from all backgrounds.
Demonstrated competence organizing and prioritizing multiple work assignments with a high degree of accuracy and close attention to detail, while meeting deadlines, and exercising adaptability to changing priorities in a busy office setting with constant interruptions.
Demonstrated competence using personal computers and software, such as word processing, spreadsheets, electronic calendars, and e-mail. Microsoft Office Suite preferred.

Master’s degree.
Experience working as an undergraduate academic advisor or student success coordinator.
General knowledge of higher ed. curricula, policies and procedures.
Experience working with enrollment and degree auditing software, such as DegreeWorks, CatCourse, Banner, MyInfo and/or relational database.
Demonstrated experience maintaining and updating websites.
Experience composing, editing, and distributing newsletters.

Possess strong interpersonal skills and enthusiasm to work with and guide students as they discover and attain their academic and life goals.
Possess the ability to create positive rapport and strong working relationships with colleagues throughout the MSU community, to include: administrators, faculty, staff, other professional advisors and student support professionals.

jobs.description:
Description:

The Residential Youth Program Coordinator (RYPC) supports the daily operations of the Fresno Mission’s Youth Services residential program, providing Christ-centered leadership, mentorship, and support to youth participants. This role is dedicated to helping young people navigate life challenges, build healthy relationships, develop life skills, and make meaningful progress toward personal growth and stability. A key responsibility of the RYPC is to develop, equip, and support staff in effectively engaging with youth. This includes training team members in mentorship strategies, goal setting, relationship building, and trauma-informed approaches that foster positive outcomes. The RYPC ensures staff are prepared to help youth establish realistic and attainable goals, provide ongoing encouragement and accountability, and maintain consistent follow-through to support each participant’s progress. The RYPC models best practices in youth engagement, mentorship, and discipleship while creating a culture of accountability, respect, and personal responsibility. This role requires the ability to have difficult yet compassionate conversations with youth and staff when addressing behavioral concerns, unmet expectations, poor decision-making, or barriers to progress. The RYPC provides constructive feedback, challenges individuals to take ownership of their actions, and helps them identify practical steps toward positive change and growth. Through strong leadership, and coaching, the coordinator promotes safe, and a supportive environment where youth are encouraged, held accountable, and equipped to achieve their goals while growing in their faith and character.

Who You Are:

Someone who recognizes the value and dignity of every person, regardless of their background, circumstances, or choices
Passionate about mentoring youth and helping them navigate challenges and achieve personal growth.
Attentive and approachable, with a listening ear and a genuine commitment to investing in youth and staff.
Dependable, organized, and trustworthy when handling sensitive and confidential information.
Emotionally mature, grounded in biblical truth, and resilient under pressure.
A compassionate leader who balances grace with accountability and is willing to have difficult conversations when necessary.
Skilled at building healthy relationships while maintaining clear expectations and boundaries.
A team player who equips, coaches, and develops staff to effectively engage, mentor, and support youth.
Committed to helping staff consistently guide youth in setting and achieving realistic, attainable goals.
Patient and persistent, understanding the meaningful change takes time, encouragement, accountability, and follow-through.

What You’ll Do (just The Basics):

Oversee the daily operations of the residential program.
Identify operational concerns and opportunities for improvement and communicate them to the Director of Youth Services.
Meet regularly with staff to review goals, progress and challenges
Coach and support staff in effective youth engagement and mentorship
Hold youth and staff accountable through clear communication and constructive feedback
Address conflicts, behavioral concerns, and barriers to progress with compassionate but direct conversations.
Monitor the residential environment to ensure it remains safe, clean, structured and supportive.
Lead or participate in daily devotionals, prayer, and spiritual growth activities.
Maintain accurate documentation, case notes, and program records.
Maintain a small case load if necessary.
Foster a safe, structured, and supportive environment that promotes personal responsibility, life skills and spiritual development.
Respond appropriately to emergencies and ensure significant incidents are documented and escalated when necessary.

Requirements:

Education/Experience:

An Associate degree in Social Work, Counseling, Human Service, Youth Ministry or related field preferred.
Equivalent combination of education, ministry experience, and youth development experience may be considered.
3 years of experience working with youth, young adults, vulnerable populations, or related human services preferred.
Experience with conflict resolution, accountability, and trauma informed care.

Requirements:

A mature walk with Jesus Christ and able to articulate Biblical beliefs and their application within the context of the Fresno Mission. All employees of Fresno Mission are an integral part of the outreach ministry of a non-denominational, evangelical ministry sharing the Gospel of Jesus Christ through transformational programs that provide food, shelter, clothing, education, job training and renewal of families to the poor and addicted. All employees are Christian missionaries and are required from time to time to participate in chapel services, outreach ministries, Bible studies and prayer times. Due to the nature of these types of ministries, it is an absolute necessity that each employee possesses and maintain a Christian testimony of their faith and experience in Jesus. Must be in agreement with the Statement of Faith of the Fresno Mission.

new_jobs.title: Solutions Engineer
new_jobs.description:
About Code Metal

Code Metal is the leader in automated software engineering you can trust. As AI writes more of the world's code, the bottleneck in software has shifted from writing code to verifying it works, and AI cannot verify its own work with certainty. Code Metal takes a fundamentally different approach: constrain AI to what it does reliably, verify every step independently of the model using formal methods, and keep engineers in the loop on the decisions that matter. The result isn't code that probably works — it's code that is provably correct, with auditable proof. Customers including the U.S. Air Force, L3Harris, RTX, and Toshiba use Code Metal to modernize legacy code, optimize performance on real hardware, and move prototypes to production, fast. Founded in 2023 with offices in Boston and San Francisco, Code Metal is funded by Accel, Salesforce Ventures, B Capital, Smith Point Capital, J2 Ventures, Shield Capital, Overmatch, RTX, and others.

Learn more at codemetal.ai.

Solutions Engineer

Code Metal is looking for a Solutions Engineer to sit at the intersection of engineering, prototyping, and customer growth - turning promising opportunities into working technical systems. You'll be a hands-on bridge between our platform and real-world use, building and validating customer solutions through proofs of concept and early development, then helping transition successful work toward repeatable production use.

Who thrives in this role:

Engineers who enjoy turning loosely defined customer problems into working systems.
Technically curious people who can quickly explore unfamiliar domains, prototype approaches, and turn what they learn into working solutions.
Hands-on builders who combine strong technical judgment with rapid execution and follow-through.
Comfortable owning the technical execution of a customer problem - from a scoped opportunity through a validated proof of concept and early deployment.
Thrive in open-ended environments and can context-switch quickly across technical domains.
Willing to learn quickly and go deep when a customer problem demands it.
A strong technical background is required, whether your experience comes from engineering, research, or other technical roles. You'll often be among the first engineers to prove how Code Metal's technology can solve a new customer problem in practice.

Responsibilities:

Turn scoped customer opportunities into working technical solutions that demonstrate how Code Metal's technology can be applied in real-world systems.
Work with customer engineers and stakeholders to understand development needs, system constraints, and success criteria, then translate them into executable implementation plans.
Rapidly investigate unfamiliar technical domains and de-risk solution paths through hands-on prototyping, integration, and feasibility testing.
Build and lead proofs of concept (PoCs), working with Solutions Architects, product, engineering, and customer teams to turn an agreed approach into a validated system.
Implement complex algorithms and compute-heavy pipelines (DSP, RF, communications, and similar workloads) on GPUs, FPGAs, and edge systems using Code Metal's platform.
Profile, debug, and tune PoCs and early deployments for latency, throughput, memory, and power across heterogeneous compute environments.
Debug across heterogeneous systems (CPU/GPU/FPGA), identifying and resolving issues spanning algorithms, software, hardware, and toolchains.
Use PoCs and technical demos to make Code Metal's product differentiators concrete and measurable for customers.
Capture reusable code, integration patterns, and playbooks from successful PoCs so future customer work can move faster.
Support early integration and validation as needed, partnering with Forward Deployed Engineers when work transitions into sustained deployment or production.
Work across Solutions Architecture, Forward Deployed Engineering, product, core engineering, research, and growth, feeding technical learnings back into the platform and customer strategy.

Requirements:

Strong background in computer science, systems engineering, electrical engineering, physics, or a related technical field.
Ability to quickly learn unfamiliar domains and turn new technical information into practical experiments and implementations.
Strong analytical thinking, problem decomposition, and hands-on prototyping skills.
Demonstrated ability to debug complex systems across software and hardware boundaries.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain implementation tradeoffs and technical results clearly to customers and internal teams.
Self-starter who can operate independently and effectively in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
Willingness to travel occasionally to customer sites as needed (est. 10%-20% travel)

Great to Have:

Experience designing or architecting complex technical systems.
Broad cross-domain software experience in one or more of: C/C++, Rust, Python, Verilog/VHDL, MATLAB, CUDA/OpenCL.
Hands-on experience with GPU programming, FPGA development, embedded or edge systems, especially where software, hardware, and physical systems intersect.
Experience with compute-intensive workloads such as DSP, RF, communications, or computer vision.
Experience working with U.S. Government programs or dual-use technologies.
Active U.S. security clearance (Secret or Top Secret), or eligibility to obtain one.

Level Expectations by Track

This role is open at Senior, Staff, or Principal level. The expectations below describe how scope, ownership, and technical leadership differ by level; candidates are evaluated against the level they are hired into.

Senior:

Years of Experience: 5+
Engineering Craft & Code Quality: Writes clean, idiomatic, well-tested code/output and follows best practices; drives debugging of the team's hardest issues; ensures AI-assisted work is correct, modular, and fully tested.
Architecture & Technical Knowledge: Designs and implements changes to single systems, collaborates on larger designs, and drives architecture reviews for multi-developer projects.
Delivery, Scoping & De-risking: Works with Product to scope and de-risk work; provides reliable estimates for medium-sized projects with clear risk communication.
Technical Leadership & Mentorship: A go-to technical reviewer for the team's codebase; mentors and onboards teammates; contributes to interviews and candidate experience.

Staff:

Years of Experience: 7+
Engineering Craft & Code Quality: Defines and enforces the team's testing strategy, standards, and quality bar; ensures AI-generated output is tightly integrated into existing paradigms and robustly tested.
Architecture & Technical Knowledge: Designs cross-cutting changes across the stack; provides architectural guidance across the team; owns design docs for major multi-service or multi-surface projects.
Delivery, Scoping & De-risking: Owns technical scoping and execution strategy for complex, multi-sprint initiatives; audits requirements for technical risk and hidden dependencies before development begins.
Technical Leadership & Mentorship: The primary technical gatekeeper for the team's codebase; reviews most high-impact work; leads technical grooming, design spikes, and RFCs; coordinates across pods when changes cross domain boundaries.

Principal:

Years of Experience: 10+
Engineering Craft & Code Quality: Sets the quality and correctness bar across the department; their work is the example others learn from; improves the automated systems and practices that ensure quality department-wide.
Architecture & Technical Knowledge: Provides architectural guidance across the department and invents paradigms that solve CodeMetal-specific domain problems (e.g., translation, optimization, deployment across target environments); a key resource on every major system.
Delivery, Scoping & De-risking: A consistent contributor to the company's technical roadmap; gives reliable estimates for large cross-team initiatives; ensures pragmatic scoping toward the most valuable outcomes.
Technical Leadership & Mentorship: An active driver of company-wide architectural reviews and proposals; mentors mid-level and senior staff at scale; influences others across departments toward the best technical outcome.

Benefits

Pay depends on experience, but we strive to be at the upper end of the salary range
Health care plan with 100% premium coverage, including medical, dental, and vision
401k with 5% matching
Paid Time Off (uncapped vacation, plus sick and public holidays)
Flexible hybrid or remote work arrangement
Relocation assistance for qualifying employees

Wage Transparency - The salary range for this role is not a guarantee of compensation or salary, as the final offer amount may vary based on factors including, but not limited to, individual proficiency, skills, experience, and location.

We are an equal opportunity employer. US Citizenship may be required for certain project assignments involving security clearance.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Position Details

Classification Title Program Coord II Working Title Program Coordinator II– Health Professions Resource Center Brief Position Overview

The full-time Student Success Coordinator provides a high level of customer service and student support to the office of Health Professions Resource Center.

Position Number 4M1731 Department University Studies Division Office of Academic Affairs Appointment Type Classified Contract Term Fiscal Year Semester If other, specify From date If other, specify End date FLSA Non-Exempt Union Affiliation FOCUS-MFPE FTE 1.0 Benefits Eligible Eligible Salary $21.99 per hour, commensurate with experience, education, and qualifications. Contract Type Classified Salary If other, please specify Recruitment Type Open

Position Details

General Statement

Health Professions Resource Center (HPRC) is a pre-professional advising office that supports MSU students and alumni of any college of degree program. The office provides critical professional support within the areas of exploration, preparation, and application to health and allied health programs. The HPRC office focuses on individualized support plans for each student that guide their academic and professional journey during and after their time at Montana State University.

HPRC is also home to the post-bacc pre-medical certificate program for students who are career changers and require a substantial amount of coursework to fulfill pre-requisites for their graduate school applications.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Student Success Coordinator is required to provide a high level of administrative support, customer service, and technical support to Health Professions Advising. The Student Success Coordinator will enhance the quality and effectiveness of undergraduate, post-bacc, and graduate student pre-professional support, services and experiences with high level advising and technical support to students, faculty, and staff. Responds and works with campus departments to resolve academic issues. Maintains student electronic files, keeping up-to-date with university procedures, interpreting university academic policy and providing academic advice to faculty and students. Other related office duties may be assigned.

The duties and responsibilities of the Academic Services Coordinator include the following:

Health Professions Program Coordinator

Serves as the primary point of contact with the MSU student service units including the Office of the Registrar, Office of Admissions, Student Employment Services, and Student Support Services.
Provide information and support to students considering a health profession as a future career.
Helps make students aware of campus-wide advising and other academic support services.
Helps students understand and follow academic policies, rules, and requirements.
Inform students of academic and student support services.
Process undergraduate student forms, including Add/Drop and Change of Curriculum.
Serve as office liaison with the HRPC team and Advising Commons.
Maintain office advising information and resources SharePoint.
Assist with office events, including Welcome Back Social, end of semester, and graduation events.
Assess coursework for incoming post-bacc students.
Conduct graduation audits, review graduation applications and certify students for graduation based on guidelines provided by the steering committee for post-bacc pre-med certification program.
Provide academic advising to post-bacc students (non-degree) and post-bacc pre-med certificate (degree) students.
Coordinate communication of information related to important dates, deadlines and procedures to advisees and staff within the academic unit(s) served.

Administration

Serves as front-line customer service; assists Director of HRPC, in day-to-day operations of the office.
Maintains schedules for conference rooms.
Researches and prepares data on academic issues such as course offerings, enrollment, and course loads to provide supporting documentation for critical pre-req courses for students.
Refer student issues or faculty questions to HRPC Director.
Manages FERPA form completion and letters of recommendation for students. Manages record of the file submission in Karatemail and updates internal databases.
Assist with the management of student data- entering students into banner for NAV and Degreeworks indicators, student meetings record, admissions data, etc.
Manages catalog revisions and course offerings in campus systems.

Communications/Events Coordinator

Creates departmental marketing and promotional materials in partnership with University Communications.
Manages and maintains web pages in accordance with university guidelines.
Assists with weekly newsletter to students, faculty, and MSU staff.

Required Qualifications – Experience, Education, Knowledge & Skills

Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field with experience working with undergraduate college students in an academic or student support setting, or an equivalent combination of education and/or experience.
Experience working with academic curricula, degree requirements, policies and procedures in a higher education setting.
Progressively responsible experience providing customer service in an office environment or an equivalent combination of relevant education and/or experience.
Demonstrated excellent customer service and written and verbal communication skills to serve constituents from all backgrounds.
Demonstrated competence organizing and prioritizing multiple work assignments with a high degree of accuracy and close attention to detail, while meeting deadlines, and exercising adaptability to changing priorities in a busy office setting with constant interruptions.
Demonstrated competence using personal computers and software, such as word processing, spreadsheets, electronic calendars, and e-mail. Microsoft Office Suite preferred.

Preferred Qualifications – Experience, Education, Knowledge & Skills

Master’s degree.
Experience working as an undergraduate academic advisor or student success coordinator.
General knowledge of higher ed. curricula, policies and procedures.
Experience working with enrollment and degree auditing software, such as DegreeWorks, CatCourse, Banner, MyInfo and/or relational database.
Demonstrated experience maintaining and updating websites.
Experience composing, editing, and distributing newsletters.

The Successful Candidate Will

Possess strong interpersonal skills and enthusiasm to work with and guide students as they discover and attain their academic and life goals.
Possess the ability to create positive rapport and strong working relationships with colleagues throughout the MSU community, to include: administrators, faculty, staff, other professional advisors and student support professionals.
Possess strong written and oral communication skills.
Possess the ability to troubleshoot problems and have candid conversations.
Experience and awareness of how to manage and maintain confidential information
Have proven ability to work independently and in a team environment.
Have the ability to represent the department, college and university in a professional and courteous manner.
Actively pursue training and professional development opportunities.
Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively with varying populations.
Communicate effectively with employees and the public, both in person and over the phone.
Handle confidential records and information.
Act as a team player, establishing and maintaining effective working relationships with co-workers and the public.

new_jobs.title: Residential Youth Program Coordinator
new_jobs.description:
Description:

The Residential Youth Program Coordinator (RYPC) supports the daily operations of the Fresno Mission’s Youth Services residential program, providing Christ-centered leadership, mentorship, and support to youth participants. This role is dedicated to helping young people navigate life challenges, build healthy relationships, develop life skills, and make meaningful progress toward personal growth and stability. A key responsibility of the RYPC is to develop, equip, and support staff in effectively engaging with youth. This includes training team members in mentorship strategies, goal setting, relationship building, and trauma-informed approaches that foster positive outcomes. The RYPC ensures staff are prepared to help youth establish realistic and attainable goals, provide ongoing encouragement and accountability, and maintain consistent follow-through to support each participant’s progress. The RYPC models best practices in youth engagement, mentorship, and discipleship while creating a culture of accountability, respect, and personal responsibility. This role requires the ability to have difficult yet compassionate conversations with youth and staff when addressing behavioral concerns, unmet expectations, poor decision-making, or barriers to progress. The RYPC provides constructive feedback, challenges individuals to take ownership of their actions, and helps them identify practical steps toward positive change and growth. Through strong leadership, and coaching, the coordinator promotes safe, and a supportive environment where youth are encouraged, held accountable, and equipped to achieve their goals while growing in their faith and character.

Who You Are:

Someone who recognizes the value and dignity of every person, regardless of their background, circumstances, or choices
Passionate about mentoring youth and helping them navigate challenges and achieve personal growth.
Attentive and approachable, with a listening ear and a genuine commitment to investing in youth and staff.
Dependable, organized, and trustworthy when handling sensitive and confidential information.
Emotionally mature, grounded in biblical truth, and resilient under pressure.
A compassionate leader who balances grace with accountability and is willing to have difficult conversations when necessary.
Skilled at building healthy relationships while maintaining clear expectations and boundaries.
A team player who equips, coaches, and develops staff to effectively engage, mentor, and support youth.
Committed to helping staff consistently guide youth in setting and achieving realistic, attainable goals.
Patient and persistent, understanding the meaningful change takes time, encouragement, accountability, and follow-through.

What You’ll Do (just The Basics):

Oversee the daily operations of the residential program.
Identify operational concerns and opportunities for improvement and communicate them to the Director of Youth Services.
Meet regularly with staff to review goals, progress and challenges
Coach and support staff in effective youth engagement and mentorship
Hold youth and staff accountable through clear communication and constructive feedback
Address conflicts, behavioral concerns, and barriers to progress with compassionate but direct conversations.
Monitor the residential environment to ensure it remains safe, clean, structured and supportive.
Lead or participate in daily devotionals, prayer, and spiritual growth activities.
Maintain accurate documentation, case notes, and program records.
Maintain a small case load if necessary.
Foster a safe, structured, and supportive environment that promotes personal responsibility, life skills and spiritual development.
Respond appropriately to emergencies and ensure significant incidents are documented and escalated when necessary.

Requirements:

Education/Experience:

An Associate degree in Social Work, Counseling, Human Service, Youth Ministry or related field preferred.
Equivalent combination of education, ministry experience, and youth development experience may be considered.
3 years of experience working with youth, young adults, vulnerable populations, or related human services preferred.
Experience with conflict resolution, accountability, and trauma informed care.

Requirements:

A mature walk with Jesus Christ and able to articulate Biblical beliefs and their application within the context of the Fresno Mission. All employees of Fresno Mission are an integral part of the outreach ministry of a non-denominational, evangelical ministry sharing the Gospel of Jesus Christ through transformational programs that provide food, shelter, clothing, education, job training and renewal of families to the poor and addicted. All employees are Christian missionaries and are required from time to time to participate in chapel services, outreach ministries, Bible studies and prayer times. Due to the nature of these types of ministries, it is an absolute necessity that each employee possesses and maintain a Christian testimony of their faith and experience in Jesus. Must be in agreement with the Statement of Faith of the Fresno Mission.

new_jobs.title: Care giver agency program coordinator or Qidp
new_jobs.description:
Company Description
Supportive Touch Care Solutions is a caregiving agency dedicated to providing person-centered support services to individuals with diverse abilities and needs. The organization focuses on promoting independence, dignity, and quality of life through individualized care plans and collaborative service delivery. Supportive Touch Care Solutions partners with families, community resources, and interdisciplinary teams to ensure continuity of care and meaningful engagement in daily living. The agency is committed to maintaining a supportive work environment for team members, emphasizing professional growth, ethical practice, and high standards of care. As a growing organization in the Boise Metropolitan Area, Supportive Touch Care Solutions offers opportunities for impact and career development in human services.
Role Description
The Caregiver Agency Program Coordinator / QIDP (Qualified Intellectual Disabilities Professional) is a full-time, on-site role based in the Boise Metropolitan Area. This role oversees the coordination of care services, ensuring that individuals receive appropriate supports aligned with their person-centered plans and regulatory requirements. Day-to-day responsibilities include developing, implementing, and monitoring service plans; conducting assessments; and maintaining documentation that meets agency and state standards. The coordinator collaborates with caregivers, families, and clinical professionals, provides coaching and support to direct care staff, and participates in care conferences and interdisciplinary meetings. Additional tasks include scheduling, responding to service issues, ensuring compliance with policies and licensing requirements, supporting quality improvement initiatives, and contributing to a positive and inclusive environment for individuals served and staff.
Qualifications

Experience in human services, social work, psychology, special education, or related field, preferably working with individuals with intellectual or developmental disabilities.
Knowledge of person-centered planning, behavior support, and regulatory requirements related to disability services and community-based programs.
Strong organizational and program coordination skills, including scheduling, documentation, and case management in a care or support services setting.
Effective communication and interpersonal skills to collaborate with individuals served, families, caregivers, and interdisciplinary team members.
Ability to train, mentor, and support direct care staff in delivering high-quality, respectful, and safe services.
Proficiency with basic office software and electronic documentation systems to manage records and reporting.
Demonstrated ability to work on-site, adapt to changing needs, prioritize tasks, and maintain professionalism in challenging situations.
Associate or Bachelor’s degree in a related field is preferred; QIDP eligibility or equivalent qualifications per state guidelines is an asset.
CPR/First Aid certification, valid driver’s license, and ability to meet background check and other compliance requirements as applicable.
Ability to build a strong connections with people, organizations, other agencies inorder to acquire new clients.
